transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, September 7. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 5-state polls set for Feb-March, with UP voting 2 months before term ends. UP 2 months early, P 14 'They're clearly hoping to kill him in there': Imran Khan's sons raise serious concerns. The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord's Test against England. Sulaiman and Kasim Khan also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison, claiming that Pakistan authorities are trying to silence him. UN-backed map must depict India's territory accurately: Government. 'Not specific map', P 9 Tech CEO added to FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list after fleeing from United States. Tech CEO Bernhard Fritsch has achieved infamy by landing a spot on the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list after his conviction for investment fraud. Sentenced to fifteen years in prison and required to make restitution, he managed to evade authorities post-arrest in Mexico by escaping to Germany. The FBI is now urgently seeking tips that could lead to his recapture and subsequent conviction. 'Win against India damaged us a lot': Yousuf explains Pakistan cricket's decline. Pakistan had never beaten India in a World Cup before that match in 2021. Babar Azam scored an unbeaten 68, while Mohammad Rizwan made 79 not out as Pakistan chased down 152 without losing a wicket. The win was celebrated as a historic moment for Pakistan cricket. However, Yousuf believes the victory also changed the mindset of the players and played a role in the team's decline in the years that followed. 6 killed in Delhi building collapse; illegal buildings over 4 floors to face action. NEW DELHI: The death toll in the Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi rose to six as search and rescue operations continued at the site, with teams clearing heavy debris and looking for any remaining trapped persons. Five dead as Amazon cargo plane crashes off Miami runway. At least five people have died after an Amazon cargo Boeing 767-300 plane crashed into vehicles and caught fire while overshooting the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, officials said. Lululemon founder Chip Wilson files for divorce after 20 years, no prenup. Chip Wilson, founder of Lululemon, has filed for divorce from wife Shannon 'Summer' Wilson after 20 years of marriage. The couple reportedly had no prenuptial agreement. Wilson owns an 8.6 percent stake in Lululemon worth nearly $1 billion, while Shannon holds about 1 percent , valued at $100 million, leaving their substantial assets in focus. Ohio dam removal doubles free-flowing habitat, 15 new fish species found. A restored Lake Erie wetland saw millions of aquatic animals after reconnection to waterways. High-resolution sonar tracked over 3.4 million fish movements into and out of the marsh. Fish utilized the habitat throughout the day and night, showing continuous usage patterns. This research provides clear evidence of how aquatic species use restored coastal habitats. Palantir-Backed Ukraine Defence Venture: Fedorov launches secretive startup. Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov is launching a new defense technology venture. Palantir CEO Alex Karp is serving as the startup's first lead investor. This initiative aims to commercialize Ukraine's battlefield innovations for allies. Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt also developed a low-cost drone for Ukraine. Agency won't be privatised or its role diminished: Isro. NEW DELHI: Allaying fears of some of its staff that the organisation will be privatised and its role reduced to an R and D lab, Isro on Sunday dismissed "speculations and misinformation" about any diminution of its role, calling such reports "baseless and incorrect".

A leadership dispute within AJJAKS escalated in Bhopal on Sunday as rival factions came face to face at its Tulsi Nagar headquarters. Bhopal Bhoj Wetland Survey Day 2: Team Wades Through Mud, Water Searching For Missing FTL Markers. The NGT-directed Bhoj Wetland survey continued for a second day in Bhopal, with teams struggling to locate old FTL and green-belt markers at several places. Shooting: Asian Games 2026 will begin in Bhopal in September. Bad Delivery, Bigger Damage: IIM Indore Study Finds Unfair Service Can Turn Customers Into Brand Critics. An IIM Indore co-authored study has found that perceived unfairness following digital service failures can trigger customer rage, erode brand trust and fuel negative word-of-mouth. Behind fatal concoction that killed 12, gang that mimicked booze by Madhya Pradesh brands. Caught On Camera: DCP Nameplate Car Zigzags Through Indore, Allegedly Hits Child and Elderly Man. A car bearing a DCP nameplate was allegedly driven recklessly through Indore's Pardeshipura area, hitting a child on a bicycle and an elderly scooterist. Madhya Pradesh Suspends Three Excise Officials Over Suspected Poisonous Liquor Case. Dry spell fears to brimming dams: Monsoon's sharp shift in MP. Brrier-free tolling system Pilot testing begins at Phanda toll plaza on Bhopal-Dewas road. Two Arrested in Wildlife Poaching Case in Madhya Pradesh. A year on, pothole on Bhopal's first cable-stayed bridge remains a hazard. Critical hooch victim airlifted to AIIMS Bhopal. Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav to begin three-day visit to Dubai. transcript.title: Business and markets
transcript.text: Moving to business, the economy and the markets. Nifty's technical setup weakens; 100-DMA key to recovery. The selling was particularly strong at the start of the week, when the index fell on heavy volume. From its recent swing high, the Nifty has now declined 3.54 percent . BVG India receives Sebi approval to raise rupees 300 cr via IPO: CEO Rupal Sinha. Facility management service provider BVG India has received necessary approvals to raise rupees 300 crore through an initial public offering (IPO), a top company official said on Sunday. Last year in September, BVG India had filed its preliminary papers with market regulator Sebi to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO) comprising a fresh issue of equity shares and an OFS. Under the offer for sale (OFS), existing shareholders will offload 2.85 crore equity shares, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated September 30, 2025. "The DRHP has been filed, and we have received the necessary approvals. US inflation data, crude, Iran crisis to steer bullion this week: Analysts. Upcoming US inflation figures, crude oil price movements, and geopolitical tensions in West Asia will be primary triggers for gold and silver prices, amid heightened speculation surrounding the global interest rate outlook, analysts said. Investors will also keep an eye on consumer price data from Germany and China, GDP figures from the Eurozone, Japan and the UK, as well as China's trade data this week, they added. "US inflation numbers would be the key trigger for bullion markets amid considerable speculation over the interest rate outlook," Pranav Mer, Senior Vice President, EBG - Commodity and Currency Research, JM Financial Services Ltd, said. US Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation report for August 2026 is scheduled for release on September 11. Small-cap corrections have narrowed to 25 percent post-covid: SageOne's Samir Vartak. Cleaner balance sheets, stronger earnings growth, and manufacturing-led demand have made small caps far more resilient to market pullbacks than in pre-covid years, said the founder and chief investment officer of SageOne Investment Managers. West Asia conflict, crude prices likely to drive stock markets this week. Developments in the West Asia conflict, crude oil prices, and US inflation data would be the major drivers for the stock market next week, according to analysts. Besides, trading activities of foreign investors and global market trends will also influence domestic equities. "This week is expected to remain highly sensitive to global monetary policy, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments. Investors will closely monitor the impact of the stronger-than-expected US employment data on expectations regarding the Federal Reserve's September policy decision," Ajit Mishra SVP, Research, Religare Broking Ltd, said. IPO action intensifies as 11 companies set to raise rupees 7,055 cr next week. The primary market is poised for another action-packed week, with 11 main-board companies, including Rentomojo, Karamtara Engineering and Kanohar Electricals, set to raise rupees 7,055 crore through initial public offerings (IPOs). The IPOs are scheduled to hit the market between September 7 and September 15, with most of the issues opening for subscription on Tuesday and Wednesday. "This multi-issue rush reflects an eagerness to lock in early-stage growth equity in young companies as all these companies are below USD 1 billion market cap at listing," Rajkumar Rathi, Chief Investment Officer at YES Securities, said. The companies tapping the primary market include real estate developers, engineering and manufacturing firms, a payments and identity solutions provider, a specialty chemicals manufacturer and an online rental platform. Wheat Falls as Traders Weigh Outlook for Black Sea Shipments. Chicago wheat futures extended losses on Friday, on track for a weekly decline, as traders weighed the outlook for grain shipments from the Black Sea region. FPIs resume selling, pull out rupees 7,443 cr from equities in first week of Sep. After investing in Indian equities for two consecutive months, foreign investors turned net sellers in the first week of September, pulling out rupees 7,443 crore as a rebound in crude oil prices, rising US bond yields, and a firm dollar dented risk appetite. The outflow came after foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) infused rupees 30,919 crore in August and rupees 20,200 crore in July. Before that, they remained net sellers for four straight months from March to June. With the latest withdrawal, total outflow by foreign portfolio investors from Indian equities has climbed to rupees 2.32 lakh crore so far in 2026, surpassing the rupees 1.66 lakh crore withdrawn in 2025. CAS fights teething troubles; will VWAP return on expiry days?. Regulator to issue consultation paper seeking comments on whether Nifty and Sensex weekly options could be settled at old volume-based price mechanism with monthly stock futures and options expiring at a combination of volume-weighted and auction prices Traders turn to bullish Chinese stock bets as AI trades crowd Korea, Japan. Trading desks from Barclays Plc to UBS Group AG are seeing rising client demand for bullish options and swap contracts tied to China's CSI indexes in recent weeks Gold Holds Decline as Traders Weigh Prospects for Fed Rate Hike. Gold held a decline, after stronger-than-expected US payrolls data raised the prospects for an interest-rate hike as early as next week. Goldman's Moe Sees 80 percent Upside for Korean Stocks on Memory Boom. A Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategist is standing by his bullish target for South Korean stocks, saying investors underestimate how long the AI boost for the nation's memory chipmakers will last. GST meet gets a BRICS break, Oct to bring real test. The GST Council meeting has been rescheduled to October 7 due to the BRICS summit. Wall Street Week Ahead: US inflation data and Oracle earnings in focus. The market will closely track the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) reports, which are due before the Fed's September 15-16 meeting Satya Niketan building mishap: 5 dead, many trapped. A five-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan, killing five people. Expert View: Selective buying under the shell of Homruz and supply constraints, says Vinod Nair. Investors should indeed be watching the Q2-Q3 effects, Q1 was not affected to an extent in terms of both GDP and Corporate earnings. India-China Corps Commanders meet in Arunachal. India and China held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in Arunachal Pradesh on Sunday. Stock market prediction: According to experts, Sensex, Nifty and other Dalal Street indices are expected to witness selling pressure after escalation in the US Israeli strikes kill seven in southern Lebanon. Israeli strikes killed seven people in southern Lebanon on Sunday. Stock market new rules 2026: At NSE, pre-open session will be different from Monday - What has changed now?. Stock market new rules 2026: Under the new framework, the order-entry period will be divided into phases, with market orders restricted during the second phase. View: Himalaya is all eyes and ears. Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL), Lupin, Tata Motors, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, JSW Steel, Lupin among the stocks likely to remain in focus. Putin-Trump-Xi meeting not ruled out: Russia. Russia has not ruled out a trilateral meeting with United States and China presidents. OPEC Sticks With Plan to Keep Oil Output Quotas Unchanged. Major OPEC nations stuck with their plan to keep oil production quotas unchanged, while the Iran war continues to shutter vast swathes of output in the Middle East. ICAI explores PE funding for consultancy, accounting. The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India is exploring private equity investment in non-audit accounting services. transcript.title: Money, tax and personal finance
transcript.text: Now to your money — taxes, savings and personal finance. India's senior living market to grow 4x, cross rupees 1 trillion by 2030, Tier II, III cities to see most new projects: Report. India's senior living market is estimated to cross rupees 1 lakh crore by 2030, nearly four times the current levels, according to a report by Colliers. The segment's expansion is drawing increased investment from real estate developers and investors, it added. AUM giants lose to smaller equity funds: The surprising gap in 1-year returns investors need to know about. A fund with a massive AUM is not necessarily the one delivering the highest returns. A look at one-year performance shows why investors should not use fund size as a shortcut for choosing equity mutual funds. 5 investment rules everybody must know: You don't need to be Warren Buffett to understand these simple money basics. Simple financial rules help manage expenses and investments for Indian households. You don't need to be Warren Buffett to understand these simple money basics. Retiring with rupees 2 crore? Here's how much you can withdraw every month. A practical approach can be to keep a portion of the corpus in relatively stable and liquid investments for near-term expenses, while investing another portion for long-term growth ITR: Have you filed income-tax returns but not received refund yet? Here's how to check status online. Income-tax refunds are issued when the tax paid exceeds the actual liabilities after deductions. Today, we look at the timeline, likely cause of delay in receiving credit, and how to check status online. Power of attorney holder slapped with rupees 29 lakh LTCG tax after property sale: ITAT decides who should pay. A recent ITAT ruling has raised an important question for property transactions. Does holding a power of attorney make you liable for capital gains tax when the property is sold? The case draws a clear line between the authority to sell a property and ownership. Can you stop NPS contributions? What happens to your money, returns and tax benefits. An NPS subscriber can discontinue fresh contributions for a few months or even several years. However, stopping contributions does not mean that the money already accumulated in the account is withdrawn or stops generating returns 5 investing choices that help your wealth grow even if markets don't behave as per your expectations Personal finance. Investing requires careful planning regarding purpose, timing and risk. Establishing specific financial goals and maintaining consistent contributions. EPFO: Don't know how to claim provident fund, pension online after EPF member's death? Check stepwise guide for families. EPFO: Today, we take a look at how the family (nominees or legal heirs) of subscribers can claim their provident fund (EPF) savings, pension payout (EPS) and insurance benefit (EDLI) after the member's death. Annual Information Statement: What AIS covers, how taxpayers can access it and correct errors online. AIS gives taxpayers a consolidated view of financial and tax information linked to their PAN. Here's what it covers, when new information may appear, how to access the statement and what to do if you spot an error. Already invested in flexi-cap? Avoid these 3 categories when adding more funds to limit portfolio overlap. With 50 percent of your portfolio in flexi-cap funds, adding another equity fund category may bring significant overlap rather than diversification. Only 25 percent -36 percent of the equity exposure may be genuinely different across key fund categories. Jan Dhan Yojana: Every fourth account inoperative, Uttar Pradesh tops list; nearly 6 crore have zero balance. PM Jan Dhan Yojana: Every fourth account under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is inoperative, while nearly 5.72 crore accounts had zero balance, according to the Finance Ministry's response to activist Chandra Shekhar Gaur's RTI application. Too much money in stocks? This is what you should check before selling. If you feel you have too much money invested in equities, it is useful to look beyond current market conditions. Instead, consider why you are investing, how much time you have and when you will actually need the money 5 signs you're building a financial empire, and you know it: Smarter money habits and better choices for tomorrow. Building a financial empire involves everyday habits in spending, saving and planning. By recognising personal triggers and avoiding impulsive decisions, individuals can make thoughtful financial choices that align with their goals and values. India's rupees 100 household savings puzzle: rupees 33 goes to banks, while rupees 39 flows to pension funds and markets. India's household savings are shifting beyond bank deposits. Their share fell to 33 percent in FY25, while pension funds, mutual funds, shares and debentures together reached 39 percent . Yet 68 percent of household wealth remains in physical assets, highlighting the long runway for financialisation. Bengaluru gamer lost rupees 28 lakh after betting rupees 2.6 crore, Why ITAT rejected tax on rupees 2.33 crore winnings. The ruling came in the case of a Bengaluru-based gamer who had put more than rupees 2 crore into online rummy and poker but ultimately suffered a net loss of nearly rupees 28 lakh 8th pay commission: Central Secretariat Service (CSS) Forum hopes panel enhances contribution, sum assured under CGEIS. The Central Secretariat Service Forum said it hopes the 8th CPC would consider enhancing contribution and sum assured under the Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme (CGEIS) keeping in view higher insurance covers available in the market. UAN, passbook, claim status and more: Labour Ministry lists 5 key EPFO services members can access on the Umang app. EPFO members can now generate, activate and authenticate their UAN through the UMANG app using Aadhaar-based face authentication. After activation, members can check their EPF balance, download their passbook, track claims and update KYC digitally. rupees 10 NAV mutual fund looks cheap? Here's why that could be a costly mistake. Is a rupees 10 NAV mutual fund really cheaper? Know why NAV doesn't determine returns and what investors should check before investing. Trimming equity exposure: how to rebalance risk according to long-term goals. A portfolio that felt comfortable during a market rally may look very different during volatility. But should discomfort alone prompt investors to cut equity exposure? DA: Andhra Pradesh to release pending Dearness Allowance instalments, hike pension, appoint 12th Pay Revision Commission. Andhra Pradesh will release two pending DA instalments, give pension hikes from January 2027, and appoint the 12th Pay Revision Commission among other long-pending demands by state government employees. EPFO to hold live session on PM-Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on 8 September: Here are the key details you should know. transcript.text: Next, science and technology. AI adoption surges, but companies still struggle to turn productivity gains into profits: McKinsey. Nearly nine in 10 respondents to McKinsey's 2026 Global Survey on AI said their organisations regularly use AI in at least one business function, while the share reporting enterprise-wide scaling rose to 44 per cent from 38 per cent a year earlier. The use of AI across three or more business functions also increased to 56 per cent from 51 per cent. Phil Schiller's App Store exit reportedly driven by wariness over future plans. Schiller reportedly had reservations about new CEO John Ternus' goal of bringing in more recurring revenue from the App Store. Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men. A large study involving more than 270,000 people has linked higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine to a shorter lifespan in men. Using both observational data and genetic analysis, researchers found that elevated tyrosine could potentially reduce male life expectancy by nearly a year, while no significant effect appeared in women. Tyrosine is found naturally in protein-rich foods and is also sold as a supplement for boosting focus and mental performance, making the finding especially intriguing. Both smartphones will go on sale at noon on 11 September. An Amazon cargo plane crashed at Miami International Airport. A plane bearing an Amazon logo overran the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday during landing, crashing into vehicles and resulting in multiple injuries. The extent of the damage or the seriousness of the injuries was not clear at the time of publication. In the aftermath of the incident, the FAA released a statement Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement. Authors say publishers seem to be claiming more than their fair share of settlement payments. A mysterious signal around Earth could be dark matter. Scientists used Earth's magnetic field and atmosphere as a planet-sized detector to search for some of the lightest proposed forms of dark matter. The approach dramatically improved limits on ultralight axions and uncovered several intriguing dark photon signals that still need to be explained. Plans start at rupees 1,000. Europe has its first commercial orbital rocket. German company Isar Aerospace has successfully launched Europe's first entirely commercial orbital rocket. It attempted to achieve the feat last March, but that lasted all of 30 seconds before the vehicle crashed into the sea and exploded. This time the company managed to get the two-stage Spectrum into low Earth orbit from a Norwegian spaceport. Travis Kalanick's Atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business. The Uber founder has said that Atoms will allow him to complete "unfinished business." Scientists find breast cancer cells hiding behind protective "shields". Researchers have mapped breast tumors in striking detail and uncovered hidden pockets of dormant cancer cells that may help explain why cancer can return after treatment. Unlike rapidly dividing cells, these quiet cells can essentially hibernate, allowing them to evade chemotherapy and reactivate later. The team found that they are often surrounded by immune cells and connective tissue cells that may act like a protective shield. OpenAI acknowledges wiki incident; plans framework to report unintended AI behaviour. OpenAI has acknowledged the growing real-world risks from unintended AI behaviour, including the recent "wiki incident", and said it is developing a framework for disclosing such incidents, which it plans to share in the coming weeks, while also working with dozens of government regulatory agencies worldwide on the issue. Boox's tiny Picco e-reader should land in November. Boox teased the Picco, its take on the buzzy Xteink X4 e-reader, back in July, but provided almost no details. Now, thanks to some reporting out of IFA, we've got a bit more info, though sadly still no price. Unlike the Xteink devices, the Picco will not have magnets on the back for attaching to TechCrunch Mobility: Tesla Cybercab hits the road , and a snag. Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and now, more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. The Fairphone 6 Plus is the midrange phone we desperately needed. The Fairphone 6 Plus feels like an extremely average midrange Android phone and I couldn't be more thrilled. The mission has always been admirable. Fairphone seeks out ethically sourced materials and offers a high degree of repairability for its devices. But the phones themselves required a lot of sacrifices, like putting up with underpowered processors Indonesia's most dangerous fires are burning underground. Indonesia's dangerous peat fires are surging early in the 2026 fire season as a strengthening El Niño and severe drought dry out wetlands that can burn underground for months. These slow smoldering fires are especially destructive because they release far more fine particles and several pollutants than typical tropical forest fires, while thick smoke can make them difficult for satellites to detect. Competitive Pokémon is on phones now, but you still need a Switch to become a champion. To get started with competitive Pokémon battles, all you need is your phone. But to compete at the highest level, like at the Pokémon World Championships, you're going to need a Switch. And there doesn't seem to be a good reason why. This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on e-bikes, power stations, and how to work anywhere, follow Thomas Ricker. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. Scientists discover a hidden problem with this popular sugar substitute. Sorbitol, a sugar alcohol commonly used in sugar-free candy, gum, and other low-calorie foods, may not be as harmless as it seems. Researchers at Washington University in St. Louis found that the body can convert sorbitol into a form of fructose in the liver, potentially triggering some of the same harmful metabolic effects linked to fructose. This lifestyle program improved cognition 55 percent more than basic health advice. Older adults at risk of dementia improved their memory and thinking after following lifestyle programs combining exercise, healthy eating, cognitive training, and social engagement. Those who received regular coaching and structured support improved substantially more than participants given general health advice. Scientists find a weak spot in one of the deadliest brain cancers. Researchers may have found a new way to weaken glioblastoma's defenses against treatment. Blocking a protein called SET prevented tumors from forming in preclinical models, while targeting related proteins made cancer cells more vulnerable to radiation. The strategy works by restoring activity of PP2A, an enzyme that glioblastoma cells appear to suppress. Human testing will be needed to determine whether the approach is safe and effective. 80,000-year-old "arrowheads" rewrite human history. Archaeologists have identified tiny 80,000-year-old projectile points in Uzbekistan that may have been used like arrowheads. Their size, design, and impact damage closely resemble weapons found much later at a Homo sapiens site in France. The discovery suggests sophisticated projectile technology may have appeared in Central Asia long before modern humans became firmly established in Europe, potentially rewriting a major chapter of human migration. Compound in blueberries may help muscle cells burn excess fat. Scientists in Japan have identified a natural compound found in blueberries, grapes, and other berries that may help muscle cells burn excess fat instead of storing it. The compound, pterostilbene, reduced abnormal fat buildup in cultured mouse muscle cells by boosting fat breakdown and helping stabilize a key protein involved in fatty acid metabolism. AI can now control fusion plasma faster than humans can react. Princeton researchers have tested an AI system that can monitor and control fusion plasma in milliseconds, reacting far faster than a human operator. In one experiment, it predicted a damaging instability about 200 milliseconds before it appeared and adjusted the plasma to stop it from forming.
